name: Faerie Grown
lines: The still water in the hollow of Faerie
The fair folk say that whatever the moon sees in this water, it keeps. Some nights you can see two moons in it.
The isle in the middle has one white hawthorn on it. In the old tales a lone hawthorn is a fairy tree, and no one cuts it.
The boat at the landing is for anyone who asks it nicely.
Silver birches over a blue floor
When the bluebells ring, the fairies are called to their gatherings, so the old saying goes; and no mortal hears them.
Lanterns hang in the birches all year. Nobody has seen who lights them.
A fairy mound: the people of the hills live under it
In the old tales of Ireland and Scotland the fair folk live inside the green hills, the sidhe, and on certain nights the hills stand open and the music comes out.
A mortal who goes in to dance may come out to find a hundred years have passed. This door is kinder: it lets you look, and keeps your time for you.
